players.note: Ernest Jones stayed hot in Week 7, racking up five solos and four assists. Jones has three spike weeks and one splash week on the season and has been one of the more consistent options at positon. The Seahawks linebacker has registered five or more solos in five of his seven games. Tap him as a top-five option for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football.

Blake Cashman continued his incredible start to the season in Week 7, tallying eight solos, four assists, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and four passes defended. The new LB1 in fppg thanks to the monster splash week to go with four spike weeks and a near miss in six games played, Cashman is an obvious must-start, no matter the format type of player, and should be treated as one. Start the Vikings linebacker as a top-five option everywhere until further notice.

Alex Singleton has been incredible for IDP managers through seven weeks of the season, most recently compiling 12 solos, seven assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss for his first splash week. The Broncos linebacker already had five spike weeks and one near miss under his belt, placing him as the LB2 overall heading into Week 8. Count Singleton as a top-five option as long as he is on fire and as a top-10 option for the rest of the season. Start Singleton everywhere for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Nakobe Dean was back at it in Week 7, racking up three solos, nine assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Nakobe has five spike weeks and one splash week under his belt and is the LB1 overall through seven weeks of action. Dean has solidified himself as an elite IDP option who should be counted as a top-five option and deserves to be treated as such for a tasty Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets.

Josiah Trotter was rock solid in Week 7, tallying three solos, seven assists, and one pass defended. It was the first non spike week in six games for the electric rookie who currently sits as the LB8 in fppg and LB10 in total fantasy points. Trotter needs to be started everywhere, every week, regardless of opponent, until further notice.

Jack Campbell was excellent in Week 7, racking up eight solos and three assists. Campbell has taken a major step back IDP production-wise this season but is still a strong top-15 or top-20 option. He has four spike weeks to his name and has recorded five or more solos in four of his six contests. His LB1 ceiling is undeniable, but without a splash week and a lower floor due to Derrick Barnes producing beside him, he is no longer locked in as a top-10 option. Count the Lions linebacker as a top-15 option for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Jordyn Brooks stepped up in Week 7, tallying five solos, four assists, and two tackles for loss. Brooks has effectively been relegated to the LB2 discussion by the presence of tackle magnet rookie Jacob Rodriguez, but he still has three spike weeks to his name in six contests. The production and obvious upside keep him as an elite LB2 play, who should be considered part of the top-15 conversation most weeks. Start him with confidence for a plus Week 8 matchup against the New England Patriots.

Nick Bolton stepped up in Week 7, racking up six solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. Bolton has a spike week in three of his six contests, keeping him locked in as a top-15 option ahead of a plus matchup against a banged-up Denver Broncos offense. Treat him as such for the divisional tilt.

Payton Wilson stepped up in Week 7, tallying three solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Wilson has transformed into an elite IDP producer in 2026 and currently sits as the LB7 in total fantasy points, thanks to four spike weeks, and two splash weeks in seven contests. Count the Steelers linebacker as a top-10 option util he slows down, including this week against the Cleveland Browns.

The rookie linebacker has three spike weeks to his name and has recorded four or more solos in three of his seven games. Tap Hill as a LB3 with LB2 upside for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jamien Sherwood was excellent in Week 7, tallying four solos, four assists, two tackles for loss, and two passes defended. Sherwood has two spike weeks, one splash week, and one near miss to his name, putting him firmly in the upside LB2 discussion. Fire the Jets linebacker up as a top-15 option for Week 8, thanks to a plus matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Quay Walker stayed hot in Week 7, reeling off six solos, six assists, and two tackles for loss. Quay has four spike weeks on the season, with three of them coming in his last four games. His recent surge of production places him in the top-15 conversation for a plus Week 8 matchup against the New York Jets. Start Quay wherever available for the plus matchup.

Quincy Williams was at it again in Week 7, racking up seven solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss. Quincy has been on fire over his last five games, producing at an LB1 level, boosting him up to LB8 overall on the season. Williams is an easy top-15 play who belongs in the top-10 conversation as long as he is cooking with gas. Treat him as such for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Kendal Daniels went off in Week 7, racking up nine solos, two assists, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, one interception, and one pass defended. Daniels has caught fire, registering three straight games with six or more solos, which helped him post two spike weeks and one splash week in those three contests. Daniels has forced his way into the LB2 conversation with his recent surge of production and should be counted as one for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Demetrius Knight stepped up in Week 7, notching two solos, six assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Knight has three spike weeks and one splash week in six contests as makes for an excellent LB2 play. Tap Knight as a top-20 option for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Isaiah McDuffie was excellent in Week 7, notching five solos, six assists, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. McDuffie played an everydown role with Zaire Franklin (shin) sidelined and looks to be in pole position to play the lead rotational role beside him when he returns. McDuffie is a sneaky top-25 option for as long as Zaire is sidelined and is a top-36 play during the byes when Franklin is active. McDuffie has recorded back-to-back games with five solo tackles and is fresh off his first spike week. Tap the Packers linebacker as a top-30 play for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Christian Elliss showed out in Week 7, recording eight solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. It was the first spike week of the season for Elliss, who also has a splash week to his name through seven games. While he is far from a consistent standout contributor in the IDP world, Elliss does offer LB3/4 value during the byes and faces very little in terms of competition behind him on the depth chart. Elliss should be rostered in all competitive leagues ahead of a tasty Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Drue Tranquill showed up in Week 7, recording four solos and eight assists. No longer a fringe LB3, Drue has three spike weeks and one near miss in his six games this season. He has worked his way into the top-25 discussion during the byes and should be counted as one for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Denver Broncos. Start him everywhere.

Patrick Queen stepped up in Week 7, racking up seven solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. It was the first splash week of the season for Queen, who had managed just one spike week all season prior to the breakout performance. Queen remains nothing more than a low-end LB3 option, but flashes like this remind us that he is an LB2 talent who has just not been consistent this year. Start the Steelers linebacker as a top-36 option where needed.

D'Marco Jackson stepped up in Week 7, reeling off three solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Jackson got the start with T.J. Edwards (hamstring) sidelined and responded with his first spike week of the season. Jackson is no more than a LB4/LB5 option, even when he is seeing starter snaps, but he does indeed boast LB3 upside. Treat Jackson as more flex2 than someone you want as your LB3 or even flex1, but there is definitely enough upside to be starting him during the byes while Edwards remains on the shelf. Add Jackson where needed, especially in deeper, more competitive formats.

Harold Perkins showed up in Week 7, tallying five solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. It was the second spike week of the season for Perkins and also marked the first time both Perkins and Kendal Daniels produced in the same week. This, of course, can be directly attributed to Divine Deablo being placed on IR. Perkins should have at least four more weeks as a starter for Atlanta, and as such, should be rostered in all competitive leagues as an LB3 option. Treat him as just that for a plus Week 8 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Tyrice Knight stepped up in Week 7, reeling off four solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Knight would have been a candidate for this column even without the events that unfolded in the Seahawks' first practice report, but now becomes a glaring sit candidate. Knight popped up on the injury report with a hip injury, which would limit his upside if he gets another start. However, starter Drake Thomas returned to limited practice on Thursday (the Seahawks' first practice of the week since they play on Monday), which suggests he will likely be on the right side of questionable following Saturday's final injury report. Knight shouldn't be an option even if Thomas is ruled out for Week 8. Look elsewhere for your LB3 play.

Omar Speights stepped up in Week 7, racking up five solos, one assist, and two tackles for loss. Speights did not see much of a snap spike with Nate Landman sidelined, as the Rams went to seven DB sets rather than expose Speights, who has been a liability in coverage, to obvious passing downs. It was the third spike week for the Rams linebacker, who becomes a top-30 play if Landman misses another game. Speights still qualifies as a flex1/LB4 type even if Landman returns, so stick him in your lineups for Week 8, especially with a tasty matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers on tap.

Yaya Diaby went off in Week 7, posting three solos, three sacks, and three tackles for loss. The sacks were the first of the season for Diaby, who had been a massive through the first six weeks of the season. The sack explosion puts Diaby on the DL3 radar for Week 8, especially with the Carolina Panthers being on tap.

Mike Green stepped up in Week 7, racking up two solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss on a season-high 68 percent of the snaps. It was the third sack of the season for Green, who is seeing an expanded role with Tavius Robinson lost for the season. Green has recorded a sack in two of his last three games and could finally be ready for a breakout now that he will start to see starter-level snaps for the Ravens' defensive front. For now, treat him as a more DL4 than DL3, but as someone who can be plugged in as a top-36 play during the byes as needed.

David Walker impressed in Week 7, posting five solos and one tackle for loss. Walker was able to manage noteworthy IDP production despite no sack thanks to the high solo count coupled with the TFL. Walker now has a spike week, a splash week, and one near miss to his name, putting him in the DL3 mix during the byes. He logged a season-high 54 percent of the snaps in Week 7, as the Buccaneers felt comfortable giving him extra burn due to the comfortable lead they built over the Carolina Panthers.

Al-Quadin Muhammad stepped up in Week 7, tallying one solo, one sack, and one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. The sack was the second of the season for AQM, with both coming in last two games. Treat Muhammad as a DL4 type for a plus Week 8 match against the Atlanta Falcons.
